traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and listed requirements in docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md are implemented and verified.
Core functionality & integration: - The ESLint rule src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts explicitly implements validation that @story annotations reference existing files, enforcing the .story.md extension via hasValidExtension and configurable requireStoryExtension. It uses normalizeStoryPath and supporting utilities to resolve paths from cwd and storyDirectories, satisfying REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE and REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION. - The rule operates on comments already formatted as @story lines, integrating naturally with the prior annotation-format validation (005.0). It scans all comments, extracts lines starting with '@story', and processes the path portion, covering REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.
Security, boundaries, configurable paths: - Security validation (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION) is handled by performSecurityValidations and helpers in src/rules/helpers/valid-story-reference-helpers.ts, together with isAbsolutePath/containsPathTraversal in src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts. These functions prevent disallowed absolute paths and path traversal beyond cwd, and enforce project boundaries using enforceProjectBoundary. - Project boundary behavior (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY) is enforced both when building candidates and when checking matched paths: any situation where only out-of-project candidates exist or an in-project match resolves outside the boundary results in an invalidPath diagnostic, as tested in the 'projectBoundaryTester' and configuration/boundary Jest tests. - Configurable behavior (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS) is provided via rule options storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, and requireStoryExtension, with a JSON example in docs/rules/valid-story-reference.md matching the story's configuration snippet. Tests cover each option in isolation and in combination.
Error handling, performance, and user experience: - Filesystem access is centralized in src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts with robust try/catch handling; all errors are converted into fs-error statuses instead of thrown exceptions, satisfying REQ-ERROR-HANDLING. Higher-level logic then maps these fs-error statuses to the fileAccessError diagnostic, which includes the underlying error message in data.error. - Caching of existence checks via fileExistStatusCache and helper __resetStoryExistenceCacheForTests implements REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION. - User-facing messages fileMissing, invalidExtension, invalidPath, and fileAccessError are clear, specific, and include the offending path and error details, satisfying User Experience and REQ-ERROR-HANDLING requirements.
Testing and documentation: - tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts contains extensive RuleTester suites plus dedicated Jest describe blocks for configuration/boundaries and error handling, explicitly tagged to this story and its REQ IDs. These tests exercise the main scenarios: valid and invalid paths, extension enforcement, path traversal, absolute paths, storyDirectories resolution, project-boundary violations, and filesystem errors (EACCES, EIO). - All these tests pass in the Jest run (36 suites, 282 tests), providing strong evidence that the implementation behaves as specified. - docs/rules/valid-story-reference.md documents rule behavior, boundary semantics, options, and examples in line with the story’s Implementation Notes and path resolution examples, satisfying the 'Documentation' acceptance criterion.
No acceptance criterion or listed requirement in this story appears unimplemented or untested. Therefore the story is fully implemented and validated.
